key_insight: WaspMOT introduces a long-duration multi-object tracking benchmark built for ecological video, exposing identity-switch and drift failures that short benchmark videos often miss. It helps evaluate whether MOT models can truly track the same objects consistently over many minutes.
problem_solved: Existing MOT benchmarks are mostly short and do not stress long-term identity preservation. This paper addresses the lack of a dataset and evaluation setting for extended tracking of many similar-looking objects in realistic biological experiments.
method: Created WaspMOT, a benchmark for Trichogramma wasps recorded in controlled ecological experiments.
Included 10 long video sequences of about 12,000 frames each, capturing sustained tracking over 8+ minutes per sequence.
Designed the benchmark to evaluate long-term object identity consistency rather than only short-term detection and association.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, WaspMOT provides a more realistic test of tracker robustness under long horizons and fine-grained identity challenges. It is especially useful for developing and comparing MOT systems intended for scientific, monitoring, and robotics applications.

paper_title: WaspMOT: A Benchmark for Long-Term Multi-Object Tracking of Trichogramma Wasps
paper_authors: Tomasz Stanczyk, Yuan Gao, Hardik Agarwal, Seongroo Yoon, Tiantao Zhang
